text:
maya: Customer (private deployment, VPC + ALB fronting Istio) reports intermittent 401s from /v1/generate. They say the same API key works against hosted API but fails when routed through their LB -> Istio Gateway -> service pod. Pod logs show no Authorization header. can someone triage?

eli: pinging infra. do we have any gateway filters that could strip Authorization? ALB usually passes it. any ext_authz in front of the mesh?

maya: Customer provided a simple repro: curl to ALB shows Authorization present, but when we curl the pod's container (from sidecar) Authorization is missing. Here's the ALB -> gateway curl they ran: 

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..." https://api.acme-private.redwood.local/v1/generate
* Connected to api.acme-private.redwood.local (10.0.1.12) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.acme-private.redwood.local
> Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci...
> 
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{ "error": "missing auth" }
```

and then on the target pod (exec into app container) they did: 

```
curl -v -sS --unix-socket /var/run/envoy.sock http://localhost:15000/listeners | jq .
# or they curl the local http server that the application exposes to show headers seen by app
# result: Authorization header is not present in app-level access logs
```

dan: are we sure it's not ALB doing header sanitization? ALB typically won't strip Authorization unless using certain rules or if forwarding to a target group via HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 translation. Also check "preserve_host" annotations and the ingress nginx->envoy translation.

sarah: we've seen this before — an ext_authz (external auth) filter in Envoy can be configured to return a set of allowed headers to the upstream. If allowed_headers doesn't include "authorization" Envoy will drop it. can you get the Gateway/EnvoyFilter config?

maya: attaching snippet from customer Gateway / EnvoyFilter (redacted): 

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: pre-auth-ext
spec:
  configPatches:
    - applyTo: NETWORK_FILTER
      match:
        listener:
          portNumber: 443
          filterChain: { }
      patch:
        operation: INSERT_AFTER
        value:
          name: envoy.filters.http.ext_authz
          typed_config:
            "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.ext_authz.v3.ExtAuthz
            http_service:
              server_uri:
                uri: http://authz.default.svc.cluster.local:8080
                cluster: ext-authz
              authorization_request:
                allowed_headers:
                  patterns: [{ exact: "x-request-id" }, { exact: "cookie" }]
```

maya: note: allowed_headers only lists x-request-id and cookie. customer says they don't have any other custom auth-stage.

eli: bingo — ext_authz is allowed_headers-whitelisting and doesn't include authorization. Envoy will remove headers that are not in allowed list. that matches the symptom: ALB sends Authorization, ext_authz validates, but when it forwards downstream it only passes the allowed headers.

sarah: quick remediation options:
- add { exact: "authorization" } to allowed_headers patterns in ext_authz config (preferred)
- or configure the auth service to return the header in the HTTP response to ext_authz's "ok" path (more complex)
- as a workaround add a passthrough header in the Gateway (e.g., X-Forwarded-Authorization) at the ingress and have the app accept that (requires app change)

dan: example patch to EnvoyFilter (apply in customer cluster): 

```yaml
# patch: allow Authorization through ext_authz
patches:
  - op: replace
    path: /spec/configPatches/0/patch/value/typed_config/authorization_request/allowed_headers/patterns
    value:
      - { exact: "x-request-id" }
      - { exact: "cookie" }
      - { exact: "authorization" }
```

maya: customer is nervous about letting raw Authorization go to services (they use ext_authz to validate). are there any security concerns? ext_authz already inspects the header; adding it to allowed list just forwards the original header after validation. should be fine if the authz service is authoritative.

eli: agree. ensure ext_authz response isn't configured to mutate tokens inadvertently. also double-check for any LUA filters or ingress-nginx rules that rewrite headers. the key issue here is a whitelist.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollout of envoyfilter/namespace default scheduled by maya at 2026-11-03T17:02:00Z

maya: we asked customer to apply the patch to add authorization to allowed_headers in their EnvoyFilter. they patched and restarted gateway pods. they repro'd and now Authorization is present in app logs and the call succeeds (200).

sarah: note for us: consider a docs blurb and a console warning when ext_authz is detected without authorization in allowed_headers. this has come up several times. filing a short GH issue to track.

dan: created infra issue: GH-1427 "ext_authz allowed_headers should include authorization by default in our sample gateway manifests"

maya: customer confirmed root cause/fix. closing ticket after a 24h stable window. thanks all. :tada:

eli: postmortem note: root cause = Envoy ext_authz allowed_headers whitelist didn't include Authorization -> header stripped when forwarding to upstream -> app saw missing token -> 401. mitigation = include authorization in allowed headers OR use alternate header mapping.

maya: marking resolved in support system.
